claims.text: Deception attacks on position and relative distance information in platoon-based connected vehicle systems can lead to vehicle collisions.
A distributed Kalman filter can estimate platoon vehicle states using only local output information.
A modified generalized likelihood ratio algorithm operating on distributed Kalman filter residuals detects sensor deception attacks.
A modified generalized likelihood ratio algorithm operating on distributed Kalman filter residuals estimates sensor deception attacks.

evidence.description: When getting deception attacks on such important information, it will result in severe consequences including collision.

With the consideration of the practical issue that a local vehicle is not able to access to global information, a distributed Kalman filter is proposed to estimate the state information using local output information.
Based on the residuals obtained by the distributed Kalman filter, a modified generalized likelihood ratio (GLR) algorithm is proposed to detect and estimate the sensor deception attacks.

methodologies.name: Distributed Kalman Filter and Modified Generalized Likelihood Ratio (GLR)
methodologies.description: A distributed detection and estimation framework using local Kalman filtering residuals and a modified GLR algorithm to identify piece-wise constant sensor deception attacks.

limitations.text: The framework models sensor deception attacks specifically as piece-wise constant functions.
Local vehicles are unable to access global system information in practical vehicle platoon systems.
